transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

Not enough evidence to name a part yet. With the filter already cleaned, the usual remaining causes are a blockage/kink in the drain hose or waste pipe, something at the pump impeller/sump path, or a failed drain pump; the pump should not be bought until those are separated. Run a drain or spin-only programme and listen near the bottom front: is the pump humming/running or completely silent, and does any water leave through the drain hose? If it hums but no water goes out, a restriction or jammed/worn drain pump is most likely; if it is silent, the pump or its electrical supply becomes more likely.
pump hums but no water goes out. loud hum with a little rattle when it tries to drain. E18 shows on the display when it stalls. so is it the pump then?

E18 suggests a drainage-time fault, which can also be caused by a blocked drain hose or waste pipe. With the machine switched off and unplugged, put towels down, remove the filter again and shine a torch into the opening. Gently turn the small plastic impeller with a finger; it should move with a little magnetic resistance, but should not be jammed, badly rattly or have damaged vanes. If it is clear and turns normally, check the external drain hose for a kink or blockage next; if that is also clear, the drain pump becomes the likely part rather than something to buy on guesswork.
ok did that. impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. drain hose is clear too, I disconnected it at the sink and blew through, and the sink drains fine. so is it the pump?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
Yes — the drain pump is now the most likely faulty part. The loud hum/rattle, no discharge, clear filter and external hose, plus a gritty/stiff impeller point to a pump that is mechanically worn or has debris caught further into its inlet. E18 is consistent with the machine timing out because it cannot drain. There can still be an obstruction in the internal sump hose feeding the pump, so a replacement is not an absolute certainty, but the pump is the sensible next suspect. FD9409 is an FD production code rather than enough to confirm the exact washer variant, so use the full E-Nr from the rating label (usually inside the door opening or on the back) with Bosch spares, or have an engineer supply the correct drain pump. Replacing it involves opening the machine and handling water connections, so call an engineer if you are not confident doing that.
